catalog.summary: Picks a value from nested option columns.

patternStatus: Both pages read on 2026-09-30 and transcribed into the design document §5. The combobox page owns the trigger and the popup keys through its tree popup section; the tree view page owns the roles, the selection attributes and the multi-select rule.

scope.reason: docs/process/build-order.md reserved hierarchical-picker for selection in a tree or a cascade, with TreeSelect and Cascader as two recipes of one core. This family is that core, and layout is the recipe. ReUI reaches the same shape: one Cascader primitive with mode drill, columns or tree.

cascader.reason: The columns a path shows, the layout a width allows, the decision a key makes in each layout, the search results with their paths and the value a checked strategy emits are the same in both bindings. Written and tested once, beside createTreeCollection, which stays as it is.

layout.auto: columns while the popup's available width holds two columns and the insets, drill below it; decided by cascaderLayout, a pure function of the available width and the column measure
layout.columns: one column per level of the path, side by side, up to the window cascaderFit allows
layout.drill: one level at a time, with a breadcrumb of its ancestors above it
layout.tree: every level in one indented list, branches expanded in place
layout.ssr: auto renders drill until the popup has been measured, so the server and the first client render agree
layout.treeDom: the visible nodes as one flat run of treeitems carrying aria-level, aria-posinset and aria-setsize, indented by --slotted-cascader-depth; a highlight painted on a node that held its children would paint over them
layout.window: cascaderWindow shows the deepest columns that fit, at most maxColumns; the levels further back go to the breadcrumb, which columns shows only while a level is hidden
layout.placement: the binding places the layer against the widest width the window can reach — cascaderFit columns and the insets — computed as the popup opens, so a path that grows never moves the layer under the pointer; the surface itself is only as wide as the columns on show
layout.crumbs: cascaderCrumbs folds a trail longer than maxCrumbs into the first level, one fold for the middle and the deepest levels; a press on the fold goes to the deepest level it holds
layout.scrollReason: The first capture scrolled a deep path sideways inside the popup. A horizontal scrollbar inside a layer is hidden on most pointers and absent on touch, and the column a reader just left slid out of view with nothing saying it was there.

wiring.aria-haspopup: tree on the trigger; dialog when search is on, because the popup then holds a text field and a tree
wiring.aria-expanded: on the trigger, true while the popup is open; on a branch node, true while its level is shown
wiring.aria-controls: the trigger names the content while the popup is open; the search input names the panel
wiring.aria-activedescendant: the trigger, or the search input when search is on, names the active node
wiring.aria-multiselectable: true on the panel under selectionMode=multiple
wiring.aria-selected: on a selectable node under selectionMode=single
wiring.aria-checked: on a selectable node under selectionMode=multiple, and mixed on a branch whose descendants are partly selected
wiring.aria-level: on every node, the depth from the root, starting at 1
wiring.aria-posinset: on every node, its place among its siblings
wiring.aria-setsize: on every node, the number of its siblings, or the count the consumer gave for a level still loading
wiring.aria-busy: on a column whose level is loading
wiring.aria-disabled: on a disabled node, which stays reachable by the arrows
wiring.aria-current: location, on the breadcrumb's last crumb

value.reason: The shape tree and listbox settled: a scalar for one choice, so a consumer never writes value[0].

selection.reason: Ant Design's changeOnSelect, Element Plus's checkStrictly and ReUI's selectable are one question — which nodes may be committed — under three names. checkedStrategy decides the value emitted under selectionMode=multiple, not only how it is drawn: parent emits a branch whose every selectable descendant is selected instead of those descendants.

lazy.request: a level on show whose branch has hasChildren and no children emits onLoadChildren (React) / loadChildren (Angular) with { key, signal }, once per showing; a level the consumer reports failed offers a retry that emits onRetry / retry with the key
lazy.abort: the request carries an AbortSignal the family aborts when the path moves away from the branch or the popup closes
lazy.reason: As tree records it: the family holds no collection of its own, so it asks for a level through the same request that shows it, and the answer arrives in the consumer's items.

search.result: one node per hit, with the path of its ancestors printed beside the label
search.keepsPath: the navigation path is untouched while a query is set, and clearing the query shows it again

keyboard.effect: on the closed trigger, opens the popup; in the popup, the next node — in tree the next visible node, in columns and drill the next sibling in the active column
keyboard.focus: the trigger or the search input keeps focus; the active node moves

keyboard.effect: on the closed trigger, opens the popup onto the last node; in the popup, the previous node, under the same rule as ArrowDown
keyboard.focus: the trigger or the search input keeps focus; the active node moves

keyboard.effect: the inline-end direction in a left-to-right document and the inline-start one in a right-to-left document: on a closed branch, shows its level; on an open one, moves to its first child — in columns and drill the two happen in one step; on a leaf, nothing
keyboard.focus: the active node, which becomes the first child

keyboard.effect: the mirror of ArrowRight: on an open branch in tree, closes it; on a child, moves to its parent, and in columns and drill closes the column the child was in
keyboard.focus: the active node, which becomes the parent

keyboard.effect: the first node of the tree, or of the active column in columns and drill; with search on, the start of the text
keyboard.focus: the active node or the caret

keyboard.effect: the last node, under the same rule as Home
keyboard.focus: the active node or the caret

keyboard.effect: on a selectable node, commits it — and closes under selectionMode=single when closeOnSelect is true; on a branch that is not selectable, as ArrowRight
keyboard.focus: the trigger when the popup closes

keyboard.effect: under selectionMode=multiple, toggles the active node and leaves the popup open; under single without search, as Enter
with a query set, clears it; otherwise closes the popup without changing the value
without search, moves to the next node of the active level whose label begins with the typed sequence; with search, types into the field
keyboard.focus: the matched node, or the caret

keyboard.effect: closes the popup and moves focus to the next element after the trigger, as select does
keyboard.focus: the next element in the page

verticalArrows.pattern: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move to the next and previous visible node of the tree, which with the active path open is depth-first order
verticalArrows.family: ArrowDown and ArrowUp stay in the active column and move among siblings
verticalArrows.cost: Following the tree's order would move the highlight into the next column on a vertical key, since the open branch's children sit to its inline end. A screen reader still hears the level and the sibling position the arrows walk (aria-level, aria-posinset, aria-setsize), and its virtual cursor reads the DOM in depth-first order.

focus.onOpen: the trigger keeps focus without search; the search input takes it with search, as the combobox page says of a dialog popup
focus.active: the selected node, with its path shown, or the first node of the root level
focus.restore: the trigger, on escape, on a commit that closes, and on Tab
focus.disabledNodes: A disabled node stays reachable by the arrows and cannot be committed; it carries aria-disabled and data-disabled.

form.name: name
form.angular: ControlValueAccessor and Validator, with required and unresolved
form.react: one hidden input per selected key, under the name the consumer gave
form.reason: The asymmetry tree and entity-picker record: Reactive Forms is an integration point React has no equivalent of, and hidden inputs are the platform's answer where it has none.

overflow.reason: Each column scrolls on its own inside the height the positioner reports, so a deep level never pushes the others out of view.

measure.reason: Wide enough for a label with its count and chevron, narrow enough that two columns sit beside a field of ordinary width.
measure.maxColumns: 3: three twelve-rem columns are 36rem, as wide as a popup sits from the control that opened it before the reader's eye has to travel; an application with wide data raises it once in the defaults

serverSearch.compose: searchValue is a controlled model: a consumer who searches on a server holds it, fetches, and hands the hits in as items of a flat list with getParent.
serverSearch.reason: ReUI takes onSearch and a debounce. The value model already carries every keystroke with its reason, and entity-picker owns the adapter shape for a remote source.

footerActions.compose: A command below the panel is the consumer's own button beside the panel inside content, or a menu.
footerActions.reason: ReUI draws a footer with actions and a flyout menu. A command is not a value; the panel is a tree, and a tree owns only nodes.

virtualization.reason: docs/component-features.md §2.10 makes windowing a capability of the collection engine. Each column scrolls inside its bound until the engine's window covers a column.
